Issue:
Refactor mutating webhooks in order to generate a patch after modifying the object
Mutating webhooks is implemented using a pipeline that generates the patches to apply to the object in order to be applied by the kubernetes server API. To generate the patches the handler have to set a `JsonPointer` to the field the handler want to change and is not really a straightforward process since it have to be checked against Jackson serialization someway. Also, if some of those handlers that are called by the pipeline produces conflicting changes we need to order the pipeline someway and maintain it, sometimes bug are not encountered until the pipeline is executed in some unexpected order. To avoid those inconvenient we want to refactor the mutating webhooks in order to generate a patch after modifying the object.

## Implementation plan

Modify the `io.stackgres.operatorframework.admissionwebhook.mutating.JsonPatchMutator` interface method `List<JsonPatchOperation> mutate(T review)` in order to accept the current object (with intermediate mutations) and return the mutated object (adding it as a generic type parameter) instead of the list of patches. A proposal is to change the method signature to `O mutate(O current, T review)`

The implementations of `io.stackgres.operatorframework.admissionwebhook.mutating.JsonPatchMutationPipeline` will then generate the patches by comparing the original object (that must be a deep copy) with the mutated one and return the list of patches.

## Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] Apply the refactor
* [ ] Tests

Issue:
Cluster pod is marked unavailable if any sidecar fails
If, for any reason, any sidecar container main process fails the container itself will stop being marked as ready. Consequently, the services that are backed by such container will be removed from the serivce's endpoints making them unreachable. This is OK for patroni, pgbouncer and envoy containers that participate actively in the service connection. For prometheus-postgres-exporter, fluent-bit, fluentd and postgres-util sidecars a service disruption have to be avoided if those processes crash. And, in such situation, the processes should be restarted anyway in a best effort fashion.

We already implemented [a script that wraps the main process and detect if they have to start it again in a loop](https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/blob/development/stackgres-k8s/src/operator/src/main/java/io/stackgres/operator/sidecars/fluentbit/FluentBit.java#L75) (like Kubernetes would do) without interfering with the readiness state of the whole Pod. Though, we are missing any means to inform the user of such failures (k8s events and sgcluster pod status). This solution just mitigate the problem since a crash in the script wrapper could trigger a service disruption too.

Seems that Kubernetes have an option that could allow to solve this problem using [Readiness Gates](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/#pod-readiness-gate). This feature allow to overwrite the readiness logic by introducing a custom pod condition that could be implemented with the local pod controller (see #331). The gate is available since k8s 1.12 and 1.11 in alpha so we could include this fix from %"StackGres 0.9". We could then monitor the status of readiness of container using status and updating our custom Pod condition.

### Summary

    - compression: lz4
      cronSchedule: 30 01 * * 6
      path: sgbackups.stackgres.io/my-db/my-db/14
```

after upgrade (pg15): 

```
spec:
  configurations:
    backups:
    - compression: lz4
      cronSchedule: 30 01 * * 6
      path: sgbackups.stackgres.io/my-db/my-db/14
```

```
/var/run/postgresql:5432 - rejecting connections

```
NAME                                            READY   STATUS      RESTARTS        AGE

After changing the value of the backup path to the new version the cluster starts normally. 

```

  configurations:
    backups:
    - compression: lz4

Issue:
First iteration at a CRD for sharding: SGShardedCluster
I'd like to propose working on a new CRD, tentatively named `SGShardedCluster` to support automatic creation and management of sharded clusters in StackGres.

A sharded cluster is a set of clusters, which are architecturally independent of each other, but are logically linked by a given sharding technology that treats them and queries them, potentially, as a single, logical, single cluster. There is no in-core sharding solution, but several sharding technologies outside of Postgres core. Our aim is to potentially support several or all of them.

It is a non goal of this issue to develop a new sharding solution or solve problems or limitations of existing sharding solutions; but instead to leverage them and create a level of abstraction in the CRD that allows for very simple creation and management of sharded clusters.

Since the process of creating a generic CRD to support this use case is hard, and may require further iterations; it is a goal of this issue to discuss and implement a first, basic version of it.

Proposed guidelines for `SGShardedCluster`:
* The CRD should be marked as `alpha` for this issue and upcoming release, so we can iterate it freely.
* The CRD should not generate any resource-consumption resource in Kubernetes (e.g. `Pod`s) but rather delegate this to other Kubernetes or SG CRDs. Essentially, the job of the controller of this CRD is to generate other `SGCluster`s (and possibly `Secret`s, `Service`s, etc).
* The CRD should make room for more than one future sharding technology.
* For this first version, it is proposed that Citus is used for sharding.

Issue:
OIDC Authentication does not work with SSL-terminating Proxy
### Summary

OIDC configuration is currently incompatible with SSL-terminating proxies such as ingress-nginx et al.

### Current Behaviour 

When deploying stackgres via Helm Chart with `enableHTTP` and configuring OIDC as authentication mechanism (AzureAD in this case),
the callback URL presented to the OIDC-Provider is presented as `http` instead of `https`.

#### Steps to reproduce

Deploy rest-api usind OIDC Authentication and expose HTTP endpoint for the service, e.g. setting  `enableHTTP: true` in the Helm chart values.
Add an ingress:

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: stackgres
  namespace: db
spec:
  ingressClassName: private
  tls:
    - hosts:
        - stackgres.example.com
      secretName: stackgres-tls
  rules:
    - host: stackgres.example.com
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: stackgres-restapi
                port:
                  name: http
```

The callback URL presented to the provider is `http://stackgres.example.com/stackgres/auth/external`.

### Expected Behaviour

OIDC should present a HTTPS URL to the provider, e.g. `https://stackgres.example.com/stackgres/auth/external`

### Possible Solution

Enable more configuration options for configuring quarkus OIDC, especially `quarkus.oidc.authentication.force-redirect-https-scheme`.
One possibility for the Helm chart would be to set this property to `true` when `enableHTTP: true` is configured for the Service.

See https://quarkus.io/guides/security-openid-connect-web-authentication#running-behind-a-reverse-proxy

The proxy and header configuration mentioned in the documentation was not required in the case of the k8s ingress-nginx as proxy.

An additional/alternative escape hatch, for the Helm chart at least, would be the possibility to define additional
custom volumes/mounts and/or adding one ore more generic ConfigMaps/Secrets as env variable sources.

### Environment

- StackGres version: Helm Chart version 1.4.0
- Kubernetes version: 1.21.14
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: HEtzner cloud

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

N/A

Issue:
Develop pod-local StackGres Controller
Currently, StackGres works as an operator, that runs as a separate pod (from the Postgres cluster pods). From there, it interacts with the Kubernetes API to perform StackGres actions, including creating and destroying pods and many other actions.

However, it doesn't have a clear way to interact with the clusters once created. In particular, it has no way to explicitly run commands / take some actions inside of some of the containers of the StackGres pods. And some maintenance operations (like for example reloading configuration files) require to run some commands on those containers.

Rather than creating custom scripts, or executing commands with the Kubernetes API, the team has decided to continue leveraging the _sidecar pattern_ and implement this via a sidecar container that will act as a pod-local StackGres controller.

This controller will expose an HTTP API that the "main/central" controller will be called. This would also help to abstract the implementation of how those actions are executed within the pod containers.

Similarly to other HTTP APIs used by StackGres, this HTTP API will follow [RFC-7807](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7807) for communicating back errors. This pod-local controller will be a separate container, where a Java-developed software compiled to native code via GraalVM will be running.

For a first implementation, this pod-local controller must implement the following operations. Also suggested implementation details are proposed as part of this issue:

* [ ]  ~~Reload Postgres configuration. Postgres configuration (both `postgresql.conf` and `pg_hba.conf`) is currently handled via Patroni. Patroni stores this configuration as a JSON within and Endpoint annotation --which is backed by K8s etcd--. Whenever it is changed, Patroni propagates these changes to all nodes of the cluster automatically. However, they are not refreshed. Implementation: ideally, Patroni's own HTTP API should be called. It exposes a `POST /reload` method that handles precisely this use case. It may also be an option to execute the command `patronictl reload`, but is less desirable.~~

* [ ]  Reload Pgbouncer configuration. PGbouncer provides a command to reload the configuration (see [RELOAD](http://www.pgbouncer.org/usage.html)) that will perform this task. This requires access to the administrative database of pgbouncer (typically called `pgbouncer`, but this depends on the configuration). Ideally, this may be over localhost using the Postgres protocol, but may happen otherwise. Another possible, although less desirable implementation, is to `kill -HUP` pgbouncer's process, getting the pid from the `pgbouncer.pid` or similar file.


One common issue to these methods is to ensure that the configuration change has been adequately propagated to the pod **before** the reload method is called. There may be a race condition here since propagation of changes via the downward API or annotations on objects is asynchronous with respect to the change operation. One way to avoid this problem is to introduce a version field as part of every configuration, that is monotonically increased whenever any change is performed. Then, the reload operations must also specify which version they are expecting the configuration to be at. The reload mechanism (executed by the pod-local controller) must check that the version of the configuration materialized on the filesystem matches the one requested via the web service; or wait with some retries until it gets updated. Return an error if after several retries that version got never updated.

Issue:
Add backupPath to SGCluster, SGBackup and SGDbOps (for op majorVersionUpgrade)
The path of the storage for backups are limited to a predefined path. We have to address the following problems:

1. Issue #1383 and functionality suggested in [this comment](https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/issues/1564#note_832735008) requires to modify the internal composition of the final path used to store backups or to be able to store other objects like SQL dumps.
2. Issue #1589 requires to be able to point to a custom path of a storage in order to read WAL-files provided by a cluster working in an external Kubernetes cluster or event one that is not necessarily a StackGres cluster.
3. Issue #200 requires to point to a custom path of a storage in order to read backups that were not necessarily being produced by a StackGres cluster.

## Implementation plan

A new `backupPath` field for the backup path in the storage under following sections:

* `.spec.configurations.backupPath` in `SGCluster` 
* `.status.backupPath` in `SGBackup`

The `backupPath` field will allow an user to overwrite (if specified) any path composed internally for store/read backups and WAL files with wal-g. Also, to accommodate #1383 and https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/issues/1564#note_832735008 the default `backupPath` to read/write backups will be generated as:

`"sgbackups.stackgres.io/${cluster_namespace}/${cluster_name}/${postgres_major_version}"`

Previous version of `SGCluster` and `SGBackup` will generate a `backupPath` field with the value constructed using the current implementation:

`"${path:-}/${cluster_namespace}/${cluster_name}"`

Additionally, following fields will be deprecated by forbidding his usage for new CR created:

* `.spec.[s3|compatibleS3|gcs|azureBlob].path` in `SGObjectStorage`
* `.spec.storage.[s3|compatibleS3|gcs|azureBlob].path` in `SGBackupConfig`

## Acceptance Criteria

Addition of `backupPath` field must allow backward compatibility with previous version of StackGres.

Issue:
Implement a correct solution for resources of cluster's pods
Currently the cluster is created setting uniquely resources request and limit on the patroni container but a correct solution would be to split the resources limit and request among all containers of the cluster's pods. We should research the correct solution to this problem making sure that:

* Pod total resources limit and request are shared among all containers and the sum of resources limit and request is equals to the one specified in the profile.
* Pod resources limit and request should be balanced in a way that respect the role of each container. We should make sure each container has the right amount of memory and cpu for it to operate correctly and at best performance possible with that profile configuration.
* Resources limit and request are correctly specified in the configuration of a profile. Currently we set a value for cpu and memory and use that in both resource limit and request, we should check this is a correct approach.

# Proposal

This is a proposal to enhance `SGInstanceProfile`  in order to set the resource requirements for containers and init containers and a similar section to include with #820 or implement with this issue if #820 get implemented before this one:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGInstanceProfile
spec:
  cpu: 16000
  memory: 64Gi
  containers:
    pgbouncer:
      cpu: 1000
      memory: 64Mi
    envoy:
      cpu: 1000
      memory: 64Mi
    prometheus-postgres-exporter:
      cpu: 1000
      memory: 8Mi
    postgres-util:
      cpu: 1000
      memory: 8Mi
    fluent-bit:
      cpu: 1000
      memory: 8Mi
    fluentd:
      cpu: 4000
      memory: 2Gi
    cluster-controller: # Could be applied also to distributedlogs-controller
      cpu: 1000
      memory: 512Mi # Fix #1566 to improve this
  initContainers:
    setup-arbitrary-user:
      cpu: 1000
      memory: 8Mi
    setup-data-paths:
      cpu: 1000
      memory: 8Mi
    relocate-binaries:
      cpu: 1000
      memory: 8Mi
    setup-scripts:
      cpu: 1000
      memory: 8Mi
    pgbouncer-auth-file:
      cpu: 1000
      memory: 8Mi
    cluster-reconciliation-cycle: # Could be applied also to distributedlogs-reconciliation-cycle
      cpu: 1000
      memory: 512Mi # Fix #1566 to improve this
    major-version-upgrade:
      cpu: 16000
      memory: 64Gi
    reset-patroni:
      cpu: 1000
      memory: 8Mi
```

If the user do not specify a container sub-section in the `.spec.containers` or `.spec.initContainers` section here are the proposed formulas to calculate the values of such sub-sections on creation of `sGInstanceProfile`:

> Those values may be lowered. Also in those cases the requests may be lower than the limit when it comes to apply this resource requirements to specified containers in order to use the shared CPUs when [CPU manager policy is set to static](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/cpu-management-policies/#static-policy) in order to be in the `Burstable` group and use the shared pool of CPUs. 

* For `pgbouncer`:

  * `cpu` as millicpu: `min(1000, floor(toMillicpu(".spec.cpu") / 16))` 
  * `memory` as Mi: `64`

With `64Mi` PgBouncer should be able to handle 4096 connections. See https://www.pgbouncer.org/features.html

> Low memory requirements (2 kB per connection by default). This is because PgBouncer does not need to see full packets at once.

* For `envoy`:

  * `cpu` as millicpu: `min(4000, floor(toMillicpu(".spec.cpu") / 4))` 
  * `memory` as Mi: `64`

Scaling connections with pgbench from 1 connection to 100 only add 1Mi of used memory to the 20Mi initially used and with another increment of 11Mi with 1000 connections. If we consider 12Mi each 1000 connections with 64Mi envoy should be able to handle up to 3500 connections.

* For `prometheus-postgres-exporter`:

  * `cpu` as millicpu: `min(1000, floor(toMillicpu(".spec.cpu") / 16))` 
  * `memory` as Mi: `8Mi`

* For `postgres-util`:

  * `cpu` as millicpu: `min(1000, floor(toMillicpu(".spec.cpu") / 16))` 
  * `memory` as Mi: `8Mi`

* For `fluent-bit`:

  * `cpu` as millicpu: `min(1000, floor(toMillicpu(".spec.cpu") / 16))` 
  * `memory` as Mi: `8Mi`

* For `fluentd`:

  * `cpu` as millicpu: `min(4000, floor(toMillicpu(".spec.cpu") / 4))` 
  * `memory` as Mi: `2Gi`

Memory usage is quite high. Starting from 512Mi it easily increases to 612Mi with a cluster of 3 instances with low log usage. So `2Gi` seems a quite safe value.

For `cluster-controller` / `distributedlogs-controller` / `cluster-reconciliation-cycle` / `distributedlogs-reconciliation-cycle`:

  * `cpu` as millicpu: `min(1000, floor(toMillicpu(".spec.cpu") / 4))` 
  * `memory` as Mi: `512Mi`

See #1566.

For `major-version-upgrade`:

  * `cpu` as millicpu: `toMillicpu(".spec.cpu")` 
  * `memory` as Mi: `toMi(".spec.memory")`

Major version upgrade will run `pg_upgrade` command that may or may not require all of that CPU and memory. In any case better to give all the available resources to this container since it runs alone and we may find out a faster alternative that requires more memory and CPU in the future.

* For `prometheus-postgres-exporter` / `postgres-util` / `fluent-bit` / `setup-arbitrary-user` / `setup-data-paths` / `relocate-binaries` / `setup-scripts` / `pgbouncer-auth-file` / `reset-patroni`:

  * `cpu` as millicpu: `toMillicpu(".spec.cpu")` 
  * `memory` as Mi: `toMi(".spec.memory")`

Init containers may or may not require all of that CPU and memory. In any case better to give all the available resources to any init container since they runs alone.

Reference: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-compute-resources-container/#how-pods-with-resource-requests-are-scheduled

Enhance Web Console's usability/discoverability of the "enable monitoring" option when creating a cluster
Monitoring is one of the most important features you may want from a Postgres cluster. In SG it is not enabled by default, and that's probably fine. It also depends on the user installing the optional dependencies that the user requires for monitoring, and we don't have much control over that.

This won't change anything under the `Sidecars` section, other than the enabled/disabled status in both the `Cluster` and `Sidecars` section needs to stay in sync.

Issue:
Refactor Backups Jobs handling
### Problem to solve

If SGBackup requires a longer than the scheduled interval between backups, the backup jobs start to stack up waiting for the job lock to be released.

### Further details

Given a backup scheduling that is too short for a SGBackup to complete, the k8s CronJob will keep launching new jobs. 

In this situation, a new SGbackup will not run until the job lock is released, nonetheless the job pod is created and reserving memory and cpu resources. Also it regularly looks it 

If the situation continues, the SGBackups could saturate the cpu and memory resources of the k8s cluster, besides, it will frequently call the k8s api to check if lock has been released. 

To illustrate this scenario. Let's say that a backup schedule is "*/1 * * * *", which means that full backup will be executed every minute, and also, a full backup requires 90 seconds to complete. 

At the minute 3 we would have:
- 1 backup completed
- 1 backup running
- 1 backup waiting for the lock to be released

At minute 10, we would have:
- 6 backups completed
- 1 backup running
- 2 backups waiting for the lock to be released

As the situation continues, there will be more and more SGBackups waiting to be executed. 

This scenario has another drawback, it affects how DbObs jobs are performed. 

DbOps Jobs tries to acquire the SGCluster lock the same way that SGBackup does. Therefore if many jobs (Backups or DbOps) are waiting for the lock to be released, then they would all compete to acquire the lock first, which means that a regular DbOps would have to wait a long time before it is executed. 

Backup Jobs has another problem, which is the backup reconciliation. 

The backup reconciliation process is performed just after the backup has been completed, in the same job of the backup. 

This dependency has the inconvenient that if the backup process fails, then the backup reconciliation is not performed. 

### Proposal

There are several alternatives that can be implemented to address this problem. 

1. The simplest solution is to make the backup job to check if there is an already running backup, if there is any, it terminates itself. Ideally, generating an event informing that a backup schedule was missing. 

This approach has the advantage that it should be fast to implement, nonetheless it doesn't decople the backup reconciliation from the backup job and it could still interfere with DbOps jobs. Therefore it could be considered as a first step but not as a full solution. 

2. Move backup logic into the cluster-controller. 

There is already an issue for this. The main advantages here are:
- It should perform faster than a shell script implementation. 
- Less interactions between pods and the k8s API are required. 
- It would allow us to make the backups more resilient to network issues. 
- It could give us more decoupling between the backup process and the backup reconciliation. 
- It would allow us to not rely on the k8s CronJobs, and use something like Quartz. And would that give more scheduling options than what k8s provides. 

Also it has it downsides:
- Adding a library like Quartz will increase the size of the cluster-controller image, and we could have to deal with native image generation issues.
- It would have more memory footprint, making SGCluster nodes heavier. 
- It doesn’t solve the interference with the DbOps. 
- it would need to have a sort of consensus algorithm in order to ensure that only the leader performs the backup. 

3. Create a jobs controller pod. 
This controller would be a container that runs in a separate pod of a SGCluster. The main idea is that it should orchestrate all jobs that are related to a particular SGCluster. 

This would allow us to implement a priority queue between jobs that has conflicts in schedule. 

For instance if a DbOps restart is scheduled to be performed at the same time as the backup, it could decide to run the restart first and then backup. 

In order to not implement the backup logic inside jobs controller pod a REST API endpoint could be exposed by the cluster-controller, which when called, performs the backup. 

``` mermaid
graph TD
    O[StackGres Operator]
    subgraph SGCluster 1
      subgraph Leader Pod
        P1[Patroni]
        C1[ClusterController]
      end
      subgraph Replica Pod
        RP1[Patroni]
        RC1[ClusterController]
      end
      subgraph JP1 [Jobs Controller Pod]
        J1[JobsController] -- http --> C1
      end
    end
    O -- deploys --> J1
    subgraph SGCluster 2
      subgraph Leader Pod
        P2[Patroni]
        C2[ClusterController]
      end
      subgraph Replica Pod
        RP2[Patroni]
        RC2[ClusterController]
      end
      subgraph JP2 [Jobs Controller Pod]
          J2[JobsController] -- http --> C2
      end    
    end
    O -- deploys --> J2
```

The advantages of this approach are:
- It frees the operator from managing DbOps Jobs, reducing its complexity. 
- Since the scheduler runs on a single pod it doesn’t need a consensus verification. 
- It would reduce the interference between backups and DbOps
- It provides more decoupling between the backup process and the backup reconciliation

Nonetheless, it comes with a big disadvantage, it's significantly harder to code which would take more time. 

4. Create a storage-controller alongside the jobs-controller. 

This component would be a manager of a SGObjectStorage, and therefore handle the backup reconciliation. The main goal of this component is to make the backup reconciliation totally independent of a SGCluster. 

This component could also solve some of the current issues of the backup reconciliation, like the unintentional deletion of backups. 

Since the lifecycle of the storage-controller is not related tied to SGCluster, the backup reconciliation could still work even if the SGCluster its deleted.

``` mermaid
graph TD
    O[StackGres Operator]
    subgraph SGCluster 1
      subgraph Leader Pod
        P1[Patroni]
        C1[ClusterController]
      end
      subgraph Replica Pod
        RP1[Patroni]
        RC1[ClusterController]
      end
      subgraph JP1 [Jobs Controller Pod]
        J1[JobsController] -- http --> C1
      end
    end
    O -- deploys --> J1
    subgraph SGCluster 2
      subgraph Leader Pod
        P2[Patroni]
        C2[ClusterController]
      end
      subgraph Replica Pod
        RP2[Patroni]
        RC2[ClusterController]
      end
      subgraph JP2 [Jobs Controller Pod]
          J2[JobsController] -- http --> C2
      end    
    end
    O -- deploys --> J2
    O -- deploys --> storage-controller
```

apiVersion: v1
data:

  tls.crt: <tls-cert>
  tls.key: <tls-key>
kind: Secret
metadata:
  annotations:
  name: test-tls-cert

type: kubernetes.io/tls
```

After that I believe we would want a flag in values.yaml that would allow us to easily turn off cert generation:

cert:

Issue:
Allow specify request and limit in sginstanceprofile for non-production
Currently sginstanceprofile only allow to specify a single value for cpu and memory that will be used for both request and limit each of those resources.

Some non-production environment requires to specify both to make it possible to create a cluster that can be deployed in node with less resources and are not critical environment.

Proposed change for the `SGInstanceProfile` CRD to allow to specify a request for resources different from the limit:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGInstanceProfile
spec:
  cpu: <string> # CPU(s) (cores) limit for every Pod of an `SGCluster`. Please note that
     # every Pod contains not only the `patroni` (Patroni and Postgres) container, but
     # several other sidecar containers. While the majority of the resources are
     # devoted to the main Postgres container, some CPU is needed for the
     # sidecars.
     # 
     # The number of cores set is applied only to the `patroni` container of each Pod while the
     # other sidecars will not be subjected to any resource restriction.
     # 
     # A minimum of 2 cores is recommended.
  memory: <string> # RAM limit for every Pod of an `SGCluster`. The suffix `Mi` or `Gi`
     # specifies Mebibytes or Gibibytes, respectively. Please note that every
     # Pod contains not only the `patroni` (Patroni and Postgres) container, but several
     # other sidecar containers. While the majority of the resources are devoted
     # to the main Postgres container, some RAM is needed for the sidecars.
     # 
     # The amount of RAM set is applied only to the `patroni` container of each Pod while the
     # other sidecars will not be subjected to any resource restriction.
     # 
     # A minimum of 2-4Gi is recommended.
  requests:
    cpu: <string> # CPU(s) (cores) requested for every Pod of an `SGCluster`. Please note that
       # every Pod contains not only the `patroni` (Patroni and Postgres) container, but
       # several other sidecar containers. While the majority of the resources are
       # devoted to the main Postgres container, some CPU is needed for the
       # sidecars.
       # 
       # The number of cores set is applied only to the `patroni` container of each Pod while the
       # other sidecars will not be subjected to any resource restriction.
       # 
       # A minimum of 2 cores is recommended.
       #
       # If not specified or if field `.spec.nonProductionOptions.enableInstanceProfileRequests`
       # is not set to `true` in the associated `SGCluster` will be equals to `.spec.cpu`.
    memory: <string> # RAM requested for every Pod of an `SGCluster`. The suffix `Mi` or `Gi`
       # specifies Mebibytes or Gibibytes, respectively. Please note that every
       # Pod contains not only the `patroni` (Patroni and Postgres) container, but several
       # other sidecar containers. While the majority of the resources are devoted
       # to the main Postgres container, some RAM is needed for the sidecars.
       # 
       # The amount of RAM set is applied only to the `patroni` container of each Pod while the
       # other sidecars will not be subjected to any resource restriction.
       # 
       # A minimum of 2-4Gi is recommended.
       #
       # If not specified or if field `.spec.nonProductionOptions.enableInstanceProfileRequests`
       # is not set to `true` in the associated `SGCluster` will be equals to `.spec.memory`.
```

The fields `.spec.requests.cpu` and `.spec.requests.memory` will be optional and their values will be the same as respectively `.spec.cpu` and `.spec.memory` if the former are not specified.

A flag `enableInstanceProfileRequests` will be added under section `.spec.nonProductionOptions` in `SGCluster` in order to be able to use the new proposed fields of `SGInstanceProfile`.

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  nonProductionOptions:
    enableInstanceProfileRequests: <boolean> # If true, will allow to use fields `.spec.requests.cpu` and `.spec.requests.memory` from `SGInstanceProfile`. By default is `false`.
```

### Summary

CABundle attached to the mutatingwebhookconfiguration's for stackgres is replaced every time ArgoCD is sync'd.

### Current Behaviour 

Every time that a Sync happens in ArgoCD all of the Jobs as part of the Stackgres Helm Chart are run. I believe this causes a new CABundle to get created and the MutatingWebhookConfigurations to get updated with that new CABundle.

This results in the dreaded `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` error through the UI and when manipulating SGClusters on the CLI.

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Install ArgoCD. We are currently testing on 2.1.x
2. Install Stackgres Helm Chart via ArgoCD. See our values.yaml file below.
3. Once ArgoCD creates all of the Stackgres objects, hit the Sync button
4. The mutatingwebhookconfiguration's cabundle will be updated and UI/CLI operations will error out

### Expected Behaviour

We expect that certs to stay the same and not cause TLS issues.

### Possible Solution

<!-- What do you think is the possible solution for the bug -->

I may be wrong on some details here, but I think Implementing https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/issues/1841 would help address this issue.

Since we're not passing in a cert or key via Helm Values (since this is GitOps and we don't want the cert and key in a git repository) the chart tries to do the friendly thing and generate the CA, cert, and key so everything can be TLS'd. If we could pass in a secretKeyRef that points to a `kubernetes.io/tls` Secret this could all be avoided, I would think.

I suspect at the heart of this issue is that ArgoCD isn't running `helm install` or `helm upgrade` like the chart expects, instead it's doing a `helm template` so I believe all of the install/upgrade jobs are running every time there is an ArgoCD Sync, and this ends up updating the mutatingwebhookconfiguration. This also causes the auto-generated admin password to be updated each time, which more than anything can be confusing.

Issue:
Use SGObjectStorage CRD for Postgres base backup and WAL storage
The proposed CRD is basically a small evolution over the currently existing [`SGBackupConfig.storage` subobject](https://stackgres.io/doc/latest/reference/crd/sgbackupconfig/#storage-configuration). The main goal of extracting it into a separate CRD is for being able to re-use and reference it from different contexts.

This would enable to support clusters initialized from a Postgres backup and WAL archive. Having a CRD that references this archive, there could be two use cases perfectly supported by this CRD:
* A user wants to have a cluster replicating from the archive, and there's an existing CRD representing that archive within the same K8s cluster (and namespace). In this case, a reference to the existing CRD should be enough.
* A user wants to have a cluster replicating from the archive, on a different K8s cluster (i.e. a DR scenario). In this case, a local (to the destination K8s cluster) CRD needs to be created, but could have the same or similar contents from the source CRD, which could be easily copied, and then referenced.

The proposed name for this new CRD is `SGObjectStorage`.

More precisely, this change would imply the following changes:
1. ~~Extract the `storage` subobject from the `SGBackupConfig` CRD and "upgrade" it to a full CRD called `SGObjectStorage`.~~ (See #1564)
1. ~~Change the `SGBackupConfig` to include a new property, `.spec.sgObjectStorage`, that will become a reference to the new CRD.~~
1. <del>Add a new property to the new CRD, called `SGObjectStorage.mode`, which will be an enum with possible values `RW, RO`. This would be useful for standby clusters, which might be provided with more restricted user access credentials</del>.
1. Create the section `.spec.configurations.backups` with an array (only allowed to have just 1 element) that will replace the field `.spec.configurations.sgBackupConfig` including a reference to an `SGObjectStorage` and the other properties of `SGBackupConfig`.
1. Deprecate the field `.spec.configurations.sgBackupConfig` in `SGCluster` CRD and forbid create new `SGCluster` using such field.
1. Deprecate `SGBackupConfig` CRD and forbid creation of `SGBackupConfig` CRs. 

Note that this scheme also allows for creating standby clusters processing WALs from an object storage that might not be the original source one, but possibly one replicated in other region (eg. an S3 bucket replicated to another S3 bucket on another region), in which case source and destination CRDs will only differ on the bucket name and region (and potentially, user credentials).

Also note that this issue doesn't deal with how to modify a `SGCluster` to support standby cluster creation. That will be addressed on a separate issue (see #866).

<del>Ideally, some strong validation support should be built into the operator to validate access credentials when creating the CRD (i.e., validate that we can read or read and write to the object storage). This will improve the current user experience of creating an invalid `SGBackupConfig`</del>.

Proposed change to `SGCluster`:

```yaml
spec:
  configurations:
    backupPath: <string>
    sgBackupConfig: <string> # this does not change but will be deprecated and mutually exclusive with `backups` field.
    backups: # The backups is an array that can contain at most 1 element to allow in the future specify multiple backup configuration so that backup may be stored on multiple storages.
    - path: <string>
      compression: <string>
      cronSchedule: <string>
      performance:
        maxDiskBandwitdh: <integer>
        maxNetworkBandwitdh: <integer>
        uploadDiskConcurrency: <integer>
      retention: <integer>
      sgObjectStorage: <string> # name of an SGObjectStorage in the same namespace
```

- [x] Implement a validating webhook in order to disallow usage of `SGBackupConfig` in `SGCluster`

Issue:
Implement "ManagedSQL" as a new SGScripts CRD referenced by SGCluster
We want more and more to offer a fully-featured GitOps approach to managing Postgres databases.

One such areas that are not fully covered is managing a database DDL, or even more generic, managing a database with SQL. While you'd normally interact with a database with a CLI or GUI client, having the ability to programmatically maintain database DDL with a CRD is a well justified use-case. The current ability to execute operations by a component of the operator make this system very powerful for programmatic creation and update of DDL.

This issue aims to capture this and define a new CRD, called `SGScripts`, to be added to StackGres' set of CRDs. This would allow to "define in YAML" commands to execute on a cluster.

Note that it won't be a goal to support DDL migrations, deltas and others --that would be relied on the user or other external tools. If any edit is performed to the `SGScripts`, it will be blindly re-executed. If it is deleted, no action will be executed.

The internal spec of the CRD would be very similar to the actual [`initialData.scripts`](https://stackgres.io/doc/latest/reference/crd/sgcluster/#scripts-configuration) spec:

```yaml
  - name: $scriptName
    database: $dbname #optional, default to 'postgres'
    scriptFrom | script: read the script from either a ConfigMap, Secret or inline.
  - name: ...
    ...
```

There is some overlap with the `spec.initialData.scripts` section of the `SGCluster` and for this reason the intermediary CRD called `SGScripts` will be created in order to be used as a reference by both `SGCluster` (and in the future `SGDbOps`). Section `spec.initialData.scripts` of the `SGCluster` will be deprecated and the new array field `spec.managedSQL.sgScripts` will be added in order to reference an array of `SGScripts` instances. `SGScripts` CRD will have the following model:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1beta1
kind: SGScripts
spec:
  managedVersions: <boolean> # If `true` the versions will be managed by the operator automatically. The user will still be able to update them. `true` by default.
  continueOnError: <boolean> # if true, when any entry fail will not prevent subsequent entries from being executed. `false` by default.
  scripts:
  - name: <string> # Optional. Does not determine order of execution but creates a label to identify this script externally (like in events and logs).
    id: <integer> # The id is immutable and must be unique across all the script entries. It is replaced by the operator and  and is used to identify the script for the whole life of the `SGScript` object.
    version: <integer> # The version of the script. Set to `1` by default.
    database: <string> # Database where the script is executed. Defaults to the `postgres` database
    user: <string> # User that will execute the script. Defaults to the `postgres` user
    wrapInTransaction: <string> # Wrap the script in a transaction using the specified transaction mode (`NONE` (The default, means that the script will not be wrapped in a transaction), `READ COMMITTED`, `REPEATABLE READ` and `SERIALIZABLE`).
    storeStatusInDatabase: <boolean> # When specified `inTransaction` field must not to be set to `null` or `NONE` and the script execution will include storing the status of the execution of this script in the table `managed_sql.status` that will be created in the specified `database`. This will avoid an operation that fails partially to be unrecoverable requiring the intervention from the user. This is `false` by default.
    retryOnError: <boolean> # if true it retries to execute the script entry with an exponential back-off algorithm limited to 5 minutes with a variation of 1 minute. Default is false.
    script: <string> # Raw SQL script to execute. This field is mutually exclusive with
     `scriptFrom` field.
    scriptFrom:
      configMapKeyRef:
        name: <string> # The name of the ConfigMap that contains the SQL script to execute.
        key: <string> # The key name within the ConfigMap that contains the SQL script to execute.
      secretKeyRef:
        name: <string> # The name of the Secret that contains the SQL script to execute.
        key: <string> # The key name within the Secret that contains the SQL script to execute.
status:
  scripts:
    - id: <integer> # Identify the associated script entry with the same value in the `id` field. 
      hash: <string> # Hash of the value of the ConfigMap or Secret referenced by `scriptFrom.configMapKeyRef` and `scriptFrom.secretKeyRef` respectively.
```

However, old `spec.initialData.scripts` section of the `SGCluster` was intended to be run only once, and only if a backup is not restored. We instead allow all referenced `SGScripts` from field `.spec.managedSQL.sgScripts` to be modified and to be applied "live" to the `SGCluster`. The new `version` field will allow to detect if script have to be executed and will be managed by the operator (default) or manually if the `.spec.managedVersions` is set to `false`. When `.spec.managedVersions` is set to `true` in the `SGScripts` following rules will apply:

* Initially set version to 1.
* Secret or ConfigMap values hash is stored in the `SGScripts` `.status.scripts[].hash` section
* When an inline value is changed the version will be automatically incremented by 1.
* When a Secret or a ConfigMap is changed, the operator reconciliation cycle will update the hash and the version will be automatically incremented by 1.
* User will still be able to increment the value manually if needed.

Here is the proposed change to `SGCluster` in order to reference an array of `SGScripts` and maintain the status of applied `SGScripts`:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  managedSQL:
    continueOnSGScriptsError: <boolean> # if true, when any entry of any `SGScripts` fail will not prevent subsequent `SGScripts` from being executed. `false` by default.
    sgScripts:
    - id: <integer> # The id is immutable and must be unique across all the `SGScript` entries. It is replaced by the operator and is used to identify the `SGScript` entry. 
      name: <string> # a reference to an `SGScript`
status:
  managedSQL:
    sgScripts:
    - id: <integer> # Identify the associated `SGScript` entry with the same value in the `id` field. 
      startedAt: <string> # ISO-8601 datetime of when the script execution has been started. Will be reset each time the referenced `SGScripts` will be re-applied.
      failedAt: <string> # ISO-8601 datetime of when the script execution had failed (mutually exclusive with `completedAt`). Will be reset each time the referenced `SGScripts` will be re-applied.
      completedAt: <string> # ISO-8601 datetime of when the script execution had completed (mutually exclusive with `failedAt`). Will be reset each time the referenced `SGScripts` will be re-applied.
      scripts:
      - id: <integer> # Identify the associated script entry with the same value in the `id` field. 
        version: <integer> # The latest version applied
        intents: <integer> # Indicates the number of intents or failures occurred
        failureCode: <string> # If failed, the error code of the failure. See also https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/errcodes-appendix.html
        failure: <string> # If failed, a message of the failure
```

The user will be able to add or replace any entry of the `.spec.managedSQL.sgScripts` array in the `SGCluster`. When replacing a value the associated status entry will also be emptied as it was never executed. 

The order of execution and rules of the execution flow will be as follow:

* Each `SGScripts` will run in sequence one after another following the order of the `.spec.managedSQL.
* If any entry of any `SGScripts` fails next `SGScripts` will not be executed unless `.spec.managedSQL.continueOnSGScriptsError` is set to `true` in `SGCluster`.
* An entry of an `SGScripts` that has not been executed will be executed only if there are no other previous entry (following the array order) of the same `SGScripts` that has not been executed.
* If execution of an `SGScripts`'s entry fail no subsequent entries will be executed. Execution of subsequent entries is performed when previous entry execution failed only if field `.spec.continueOnError` is set to `true` in `SGScripts`.
* If any entry of an `SGScripts` has been already executed it will not be re-executed even if it failed.
* An entry is detected as "not being executed" if the entry version is missing from the status or different than the entry version in the status.

Issue:
Support user-supplied sidecars for SGCluster pods
Some applications might want to access Postgres, or its filesystem, or part of other components, directly (i.e. not through the Postgres wire protocol). For this cases, highly user dependent, we might want to add the possibility to "inject" a user sidecar into the SGCluster pods.

This could potentially imply many options like:
*  Container image.
*  Annotations.
*  Environment variables, config maps?
*  Inject some additional env vars to the container, like the postgres superuser and password.
*  Potentially access the Postgres filesystem (PGDATA) and/or the logs, etc.
*  Resource limits for the user-added sidecar, to control its potential impact.

# Proposal

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  postgresServices:
    primary:
      customPorts: # The list of extra ports that will be exposed by the primary service
      - <ServicePort> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#serviceport-v1-core
    replicas:
      customPorts: # The list of extra ports that will be exposed by the replicas service
      - <ServicePort> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#serviceport-v1-core
  pods:
    customVolumes:
    - <Volume> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#volume-v1-core
    customInitContainers:
    - <Container> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#container-v1-core
    customContainers:
    - <Container> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#container-v1-core
```

Sections `.spec.postgresServices.primary.customPorts` and `.spec.postgresServices.replicas.customPorts` will allow to expose any custom service defined by a custom sidecars. We may think about renaming section `.spec.postgresServices` to `.spec.services` in a future version of `SGCluster` CRD since we will expose ports from custom containers and user may not want to expose Postgres ports at all but just those of their custom services.

The `.spec.pods.customContainers[]` and `.spec.pods.customInitContainers[]` are the same as the `Container` object present in the Pod resource under section `.spec.containers[]` and `.spec.initContainers[]`.

The `.name` field in `Container` object will forbid using any container name that is used by StackGres.

~~We will forbid following fields:

* `.securityContext`: The users of the container will use the main security context and will be replaced by mounting `/etc/passwd`, `/etc/shadow`, `/etc/groups` and `/etc/gshadow`. This will allow to use postgres UNIX socket and the data volume with the same user as postgres. Also it will allow to use the same container in OpenShift with arbitrary user ids.
* `.stdin`: This will be left unset
* `.stdinOnce`: This will be left unset
* `.terminationMessagePath`: This will be left unset
* `.terminationMessagePolicy`: This will be left unset
* `.tty`: This will be left unset
* `.volumeDevices`: This will be left unset since StatefulSet can not work with it.
* `.resources`: This will be handled by `SGInstanceProfile` (see also #144) and first implementation should be the same as for other containers and init containers other than `patroni`. We will open an issue to implement resources for custom containers.~~

> Instead of forbidding we should document the fields that should not be touch and why. This is a very advanced feature and user that does not know how to define correctly a container and how StackGres internal works will be warned that using such feature may break the cluster in unexpected ways.

We may ~~also forbid~~ reduce definition of following fields in the UI to make a first implementation easier:

* `.lifecycle`
* `.startupProbe`
* `.readinessProbe`
* `.livenessProbe`

User will be able to use any volume that is defined in the StatefulSet including the data PV by setting the section `.volumeMounts[]` in `Container` object. To use the custom volumes defined in the section `.spec.pods.customVolumes` the names user in the `.volumeMounts[]` section of `Container` object will have to be prepended by the `custom-` prefix string (this is to avoid collisions). This will be documented properly in the `SGCluster` CRD to specify the names of such container and what they do.

The `.name` and `.ports[].name` fields of `Container` object as the `.name` and `.targetPort` fields of `ServicePort` object will also be prepended with the `custom-` string prefix to avoid collisions.

Issue:
Add support for cascading, remote and WAL-based SGCluster replication
After #864 is implemented, `SGCluster` would have support for replication (sub)groups within the `SGCluster` itself, allowing for different combinations of replication mechanism (async, sync, etc) and HA/read-only replicas. But these subgroups at the end belong to the same cluster, with a single primary, and all replicas replicate from it. With cascading replication, we create another whole cluster that will replicate from the first cluster, creating a two-level (or obviously multi-level) replication topology (a tree). For this case, replication groups do not provide enough coverage for this, and it is proposed that we use more than one `SGCluster` (basically, one `SGCluster` for every node of the replication topology tree).

The goal of this issue is to add support for the `SGCluster` for the following use cases:

* Support cascading replication within the same K8s cluster. A secondary (or more) `SGCluster` could be created that will replicate from the primary `SGCluster`. The primary would be pointed just by providing as a reference its name.

* Support cascading replication from a different namespace and/or K8s cluster. This is mostly considered for DR (Disaster Recovery) scenarios. A secondary `SGCluster` will be created, and will replicate from the primary cluster that would be identified by its `(host,port,user,password)` credentials.

* Support replication from a WAL archive. A secondary `SGCluster` will be created, and a reference to a `SGObjectStorage` will be added, so that Postgres may replicate from it. Note that this option may be complementary of the above two or even on a primary `SGCluster`: in other words, any replica of any cluster, may be able to combine both streaming replication and replication from a `SGObjectStorage`, which would be used as a backup mechanism.

To support this, it is proposed to add `.spec.replicateFrom` section to the `SGCluster` with the following properties:
* `.sgCluster`: Another document. If present, it signals that this cluster will not have a primary (at least at creation time) and would also imply that `.initialData` cannot be present, they are exclusive. Fields:
    * `.name`: name of a local `SGCluster` (must exist, have a primary and be on the same namespace)
    * `.external`: section with external configuration parameters. Conflicts with `.name`. Properties: `.host`, `.port` and `.secretKeyReference` section (with `.name` and `.key` that point to a `Secret` on the same namespace) for the replication user/password.
* `.sgObjectStorage`: this option may be present on any cluster (primary or otherwise), and may also be present in the presence of the above `.sgCluster` field. It should be a valid reference to a `SGObjectStorage` in the same namespace.


```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  replicateFrom:
    instance:
      sgCluster: <string> # name of an existing SGCluster in the same namespace.
      external:
        host: <string> # the external instance hostname
        port: <integer> # the external instance port
    storage:
      sgObjectStorage: <string> # The name of a SGObjectStorage in the same namespace.
      path: <string> # The path to read the WAL files from inside the referenced SGObjectStorage
    users:
      superuser:
        user:
          name: <string> # The secret containing the username value
          key: <string> # The key of the secret containing the username value
        password:
          name: <string> # The secret containing the password value
          key: <string> # The key of the secret containing the password value
      replication:
        user:
          name: <string> # The secret containing the username value
          key: <string> # The key of the secret containing the username value
        password:
          name: <string> # The secret containing the password value
          key: <string> # The key of the secret containing the password value
      authenticator:
        user:
          name: <string> # The secret containing the username value
          key: <string> # The key of the secret containing the username value
        password:
          name: <string> # The secret containing the password value
          key: <string> # The key of the secret containing the password value
```

If `.spec.replicateFrom` section is specified, it signals that this cluster will not have a primary (at least at creation time) and would also imply that `.initialData` cannot be present, they are exclusive.

Issue:
Rollback to previous version (if possible) when major version upgrade fails
### Problem to solve

Whenever a major version upgrade operation fails the user is not able to rollback the operation. Currently the only workaround is to follow the procedure to ["Reconvery PGDATA from existing volume"](https://stackgres.io/doc/latest/runbooks/recover-pgdata-from-existing-volume/) documented in a StackGres runbook.

### Further details

When a major version upgrade operation fails, if the user did not used the link or clone options the old data is not lost but is still present in the Persistent Volume. The problem is that the cluster can not be used due to the following reasons:

* The `.status.dbOps.majorVersionUpgrade` section is used by the operator to know that the major-version-upgrade init container has to be created. The container blocks the cluster from starting
* The `.spec.postgres.version` can not be changed directly by the user but have to be modified by the SGDbOps generated serviceaccount.

### Proposal

Make the SGDbOps major version upgrade operation to automatically rollback the operation in case of failure is the clone or link options are not used or only the check has been executed.

## Testing

Improve major version upgrade test in order to check the rollback is performed if the operation fails

## Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] Implementation
* [ ] Test
* [ ] Documentation

### Links / references

https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/pgupgrade.html

Babelfish Compass REST API
### Problem to solve

We want to integrate [Babelfish Compass](https://github.com/babelfish-for-postgresql/babelfish_compass) into the StackGres REST API in order to be able to asses compatibility of SQL Server schema with [Babelfish for PostgreSQL](https://github.com/babelfish-for-postgresql). 

### Further details

Babelfish Compass generates from an SQL source file a series HTLMs files with logs of the performed operations, the report and the SQL source file provided.

### Proposal

The `/stackgres/application` REST API (see #1536) will have to return `{name: "babelfish-compass", publisher: "com.ongres"}` when env var `APPLICATION_BABELFISH_COMPASS` is not set to `true`.

A new REST API endpoint `/stackgres/application/com.ongres/babelfish-compass` will be created.

The endpoint will be disabled when env var `APPLICATION_BABELFISH_COMPASS` is not set to `true`.

The endpoint will accept the POST method with a payload consisting of an SQL file. A ConfigMap with the SQL file will be created together with a Job that will generate the report using the SQL file from the ConfigMap. The same ConfigMap will be updated by the Job with the resulting HTML report, the HTML with the source SQL and the HTML with the logs of the operation. The REST API will return the following JSON object with a 200 HTTP code:

```yaml
report: <string> # HTML with the report
logs: <string> # HTML with the logs
source: <string> # HTML with the source SQL
```

On error operation the REST API will return the following JSON object with a 500 HTTP code:

```yaml
type: <string>
title: <string>
detail: <string> # the logs
status: <integer>
fields:
- <string>
```

The `APPLICATION_BABELFISH_COMPASS` will be configurable using the StackGres helm chart parameter `application[0].babelfish-compass`

Issue:
Add support for using a separate webui secret for authentication in operator Helm chart
### Problem to solve

Secrets currently are being written to disk using the Helm chart if the templates and values are rendered to disk

e.g:
```
VERSION=1.1.0
helm template \
    -n stackgres stackgres-operator \
    "https://stackgres.io/downloads/stackgres-k8s/stackgres/${VERSION}/helm/stackgres-operator.tgz" \
      > ./stackgres-operator.yaml
grep password ./stackgres-operator.yaml
```

### Further details

If a manifest is templated/rendered out, secrets are written to disk.
By providing a way to use an external secret it will safer.

### Proposal

Add the following fields to set a different secret to use.
```yaml
authentication:
  secretRef:
    name: ""
```

### Testing

Prepare namespace and auth secret
```
mkdir -p stackgres
kubectl create namespace stackgres --dry-run=client -o yaml \
  | kubectl apply -f -
PASSWORD=$(tr -cd '[:alnum:]' < /dev/urandom | fold -w40 | head -n1)
kubectl -n stackgres create secret generic stackgres-custom-auth \
    --from-literal=k8sUsername=admin \
    --from-literal=password="$(echo "${PASSWORD}" | sha256sum)" \
    --from-literal=clearPassword="${PASSWORD}" \
    --dry-run=client \
    -o yaml \
    | kubectl apply -f -
```

Render Helm chart
```
VERSION=1.1.0
helm template \
    -n stackgres stackgres-operator \
    --set authentication.secretRef.name=stackgres-custom-auth \
    "${PWD}" \
      > ./stackgres/stackgres-operator.yaml
```

Install StackGres
```
kubectl -n stackgres apply -f ./stackgres/stackgres-operator.yaml
```

Get the secret
```
kubectl -n stackgres get secret stackgres-custom-auth -o=jsonpath='{.data.clearPassword}' | base64 -d ; echo
```

Connect and login to StackGres
```
kubectl -n stackgres port-forward svc/stackgres-restapi 8443:443
...
```

A secretRef is provided in the Helm chart and used instead of the Helm values managed one

Issue:
Set restore_command when backup is enabled
### Problem to solve

Whan an `SGCluster` is configured with backups a replica is not able to use the backup storage in order to pull required WAL files in case the primary has removed them. 

### Proposal

To allow a replica catch-up when it requires WAL files that have been removed on the primary the parameter [restore_command](https://postgresqlco.nf/doc/en/param/restore_command/) can be set to use `wal-g` to retrieve the files from the remote storage. The value to be used should be:

```
restore_command: 'exec-with-env "${BACKUP_ENV}" -- wal-g wal-fetch %f %p'
```

Since `BACKUP_ENV` env var is not available in the `restore_command` context (postgres remove all env var in such context for security reasons) its value should be replaced in code with the value hold by Java enum `io.stackgres.common.ClusterStatefulSetEnvVars.BACKUP_ENV`.

### Testing

Create an E2E test to test (or modify an existing one in order to also test) the following scenario:

1. Create a cluster with 2 instances and backup configured
2. Reduce the instances to 1
3. Create a table with some data
4. Rotate the WALs until a new created one is removed
5. Set instances to 2
6. Check that the replica is able to catch-up and the table has all the added data.

## Acceptance Criteria

The replica is able to catch-up after the primary lost the required WAL files.

### Links / references

* https://postgresqlco.nf/doc/en/param/shared_preload_libraries/
* https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html

When deleting primary pod cluster may become unresponsive
### Summary

When deleting the primary Pod when this is not the pod at index 0 of the StatefulSet and there is any missing Pod at previous indexes the primary Pod will not be restarted.

### Current Behaviour 

The Pod at the missing index previous to the deletet primary Pod index is started.

This is due to implementation from #89 that, to avoid primary disruption on scale down, changes the labels of the primary Pod in order to be considered out of the StatefulSet control if the index is greather than 0 and less than the number of replicas of the StatefulSet minus 1.

#### Steps to reproduce

3. Change the cluster to have 1 instance

6. Perform a checkpoint
7. Delete the instance at index 1

The previous primary Pod is started.

Following procedure have been tested with success:

1. The primayr Pod is not the first Pod of the StatefulSet (should appear as the last element of the array in the `.metadata.annotations.history` field.
1. The primary Pod is deleted
1. The StatefulSet is re-created with the `.spec.podManagementPolicy` set to `Parallel`, adding an entry to `.spec.template.spec.nodeSelector` in order to make the new created Pod not scheduled (for example `{"unschedule":"true"}`) and set `.spec.replicas` in order to allow creation of Pods before the last primary Pod in history.

1. Set the label `.metadata.labels.disruptible` to `false` for the last primary Pod in history.
1. The StatefulSet is re-created with the `.spec.podManagementPolicy` set to `OrderedReady` and set `.spec.replicas` as in step 1.

Conversion webhooks are not tested under E2E tests for conversion from previous versions to latest version. 

> **NOTE**: Since conversion from previous version to latest version is performed during upgrade and, if it fails, the whole upgrade will fail. For such reason the conversion from previous version to latest version is not missing.

The test should try to retrieve the CR in every previous version after the upgrade. Since after upgrade all CRs will be stored with the latest version reading it with a previous version will trigger the conversion webhook. To perform such test the following shell script can be added as a `run_test` in `dbops_security_upgrade`:

```shell
check_previous_versions_conversion_webhooks() {
  kubectl proxy --port=9090 &
  KUBECTL_PROXY_PID=$!
  trap_kill "$KUBECTL_PROXY_PID"
  ANY_CONVERSION_FAILED=false
  for CRD_NAME in sgclusters sginstanceprofiles \
    sgpgconfigs sgpoolconfigs sgbackupconfigs \
    sgbackups sgdbops sgdistributedlogs
  do
    for PREVIOUS_API_VERSION in $(kubectl get crd "$CRD_NAME.stackgres.io" \
      -o=jsonpath='{ .spec.versions[?(@.storage != true)].name }')
    do
      if curl -f -s -k -X GET  -H "Accept: application/json" \
        "http://localhost:9090/apis/stackgres.io/$PREVIOUS_API_VERSION/$CRD_NAME" > /dev/null
      then
        echo "SUCCESS. $CRD_NAME.stackgres.io can be converted from $PREVIOUS_API_VERSION"
      else
        echo "FAIL. $CRD_NAME.stackgres.io can not be converted from $PREVIOUS_API_VERSION"
        ANY_CONVERSION_FAILED=true
      fi
    done
  done
  kill "$KUBECTL_PROXY_PID"
  if "$ANY_CONVERSION_FAILED"
  then
    return 1
  fi
}
```

If any conversoin webhook from the previous version fail the `dbops_security_upgrade` E2E test should fail.

Issue:
Refactor SGCluster CRD to support sychronous replication and (sub)groups roles
Within a cluster, we may support replicas fulfilling different roles:
* Replicas for high availability (i.e., ready to be promoted to primary). ~~These replicas should have identical configuration and resources as the primary node.~~
* Replicas for read scaling, serving read-only queries, and exposed via a load-balanced service. ~~These replicas may have different configuration and resources as those use for HA.~~
* Replicas that serve both cases above.
* ~~Replicas that serve none (could be used for cascading replication).~~

As of now, we only support the third case, which is nonetheless the most usual one. However, for certain scenarios, you might want to serve the other cases. Or support different subsets of replicas with different roles. The goal of this issue is to support all these cases.

To do this, I propose to refactor `SGCluster` adding the concept of "replica groups": a set of one or more nodes (pods), with an assigned role as per the above, ~~which might also be backed by different configurations and or resources~~. ~~Indeed, each replica group will be backed by its own StatefulSet.~~

Also, we're using `asynchronous` replication for cluster creation in `SGCluster`, since this is Patroni's default. All the SG supported versions have the option for synchronous replication, and [Patroni supports it too](https://patroni.readthedocs.io/en/latest/replication_modes.html).

The user may change the replication `mode` and (in the future) set additional properties, like `maximum_lag_on_failover` or `check_timeline`. Also note that `sync_strict` corresponds to Patroni's `synchronous_mode=on`.

More precisely, it is proposed to introduce a new field `SGCluster.replication` that will be an object with the following structure:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  replication:
    role: <string> # enum with possible values: `HA` or `HA_READ` (default). The primary instance will be elected among all the replication groups that are either `HA` or `HA_READ`. The role will be implemented via Patroni tags, and only `HA_READ` will be exposed via the `-replicas` K8s service.
    mode: <string> # enum with values `ASYNC` (default), `SYNC` or `SYNC_STRICT`
    syncNodeCount: <integer> # Number of synchronous standby databases. It is set to 1 by default. Only setteable if mode is SYNC or SYNC_STRICT
    groups: # if groups is not specified or empty all instances will have role `HA_READ`.
    - name: <string> # The name of the group. If not set will default to the `group-<index>`.
      role: <string> # enum with possible values: `HA`, `READONLY`, `HA_READ` (default) and `NONE`. The primary instance will be elected among all the replication groups that are either `HA` or `HA_READ`. The role will be implemented via Patroni tags, and only those with `READONLY` or `HA_READ` will be exposed via the `-replicas` K8s service.
      instances: <integer> # number of instances of this group not included in `.spec.instances`. Each replication group may set independently the number of replicas within that group.
```

The total number of instances be equals to `.spec.instances` plus the sum of `.spec.replication.groups[].instances`.

The first group in `.spec.replication.groups[]` is implicitly the second one.

For example, an existing CRD could be easily converted to this new proposal like in:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
metadata:
  name: onereplicagroup
spec:
  postgresVersion: '12.3'
  instances: 3
  replication:
    mode: ASYNC
  sgInstanceProfile: 'size-small'
  pods:
    persistentVolume:
      size: '10Gi'
  configurations:
    sgPostgresConfig: 'pgconfig1'
    sgPoolingConfig: 'poolconfig1'        
    sgBackupConfig: 'backupconfig1'
  initialData:
    - name: create-pgbench-database
      script: |
        create database pgbench owner pgbench;
  prometheusAutobind: true
```

A more advanced example could be:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
metadata:
  name: tworeplicagroups
spec:
  postgresVersion: '12.3'
  instances: 3
  replication:
    role: HA
    mode: SYNC_STRICT
    groups:
    - role: READONLY
      instances: 6
  sgInstanceProfile: 'size-small'
  pods:
    persistentVolume:
      size: '10Gi'
  configurations:
    sgPostgresConfig: 'pgconfig1'
    sgPoolingConfig: 'poolconfig1'        
    sgBackupConfig: 'backupconfig1'
  initialData:
    - name: create-pgbench-database
      script: |
        create database pgbench owner pgbench;
  prometheusAutobind: true
```

Issue:
Allow to copy backups across namespaces
Backups (either manual or managed) are tied to a given namespace. It doesn't matter which cluster they belonged to, as long as those clusters were part of the same namespace. And then restoring a backup, it can only be present in the same namespace.

However, if permissions allow for this, a user may want to restore a backup into another namespace. Since we don't allow for this, this issue tackles copying a backup to another namespace to enable a backup to be effectively restored in another namespace.

The feature will work by just copying the CR backup and with minimal modifications, not the actual backup files (i.e., it will point to the same resources). Considerations for this feature:

*  The copied backup CR will have to point to the cluster using `<cluster namespace>.<cluster name>` syntax in order to allow the backup to point correctly to the stored backup.
*  ~~The copied backup CR will be marked as permanent (i.e. not `subjectToRetentionPolicy`), even if the source CR was a managed one.~~
*  The algorithm to delete the backup resources when a CR needs to be changed. Now, many CRs may point to the same underlying resources, the backup itself, and those can only be deleted when the last CR is deleted.
*  ~~To implement the above, we'd need to implement reference counting (could be a status field in the backup CR with the number of times the physical backup is referenced) or maybe a global `ConfigMap` with the reference counting of every existing backup, managed by StackGres controller.~~
*  ~~We may need to verify that the user has permissions to create a CR on the destination namespace.~~

-----------

> The goal is to support "Backup CR cloning". This feature enables a single ("call it physical") backup to be referenced from potentially more than one CR. If either of the CRs or the backup itself are deleted, everything else is also expected to be deleted. A backup may be restored by referencing either of the existing CR UIDs pointing to it.
> We need to be able to augment the current CRD of backup to include an optional field "cloneFromBackup: $UID". Then the user can specify the resulting name and optionally the namespace of the cloned backup. The `cloneFromBackup` field would be exclusive to the current `sgCluster`.

Issue:
Support ARM64 when installing extensions
Currently when extensions are installed the architecture used is always x86_64 (aka amd64). This makes impossible the installation of extensions on arm64.

## Implementation plan

The selection of the extension in the mutating webhook must be independent of architecture on first creation of the cluster since, until the first primary Pod is elected, the architecture is unknown to the operator. In such case extensions will be chosen only based on name, version, postgres version and flavor.

When the extension is then installed in the Pod the architecture will be resolved by the cluster controller.

When the primary pod is elected and ready the cluster controller of such Pod will set the architecture in the `SGCluster` under `.status.primaryArch`.

When the mutating webhook check extensions, will be able to filter by architecture when the `.status.primaryArch` is set in `SGCluster` using such value. Since [postgres does not support streaming replication between different architectures](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/59264875/replicating-a-postgresql-database-when-master-is-running-on-arm-and-replication) all the extensions that will be installed on the cluster will always have the same architecture.

## Acceptance Criteria

When creating an `SGCluster` the first time the architecture will not be used to filter extensions. When adding extensions they will be filtered by architecture when the `.status.primaryArch` is set in `SGCluster` using such value.
The cluster controller will detect the architeture where it is running, will use the detected architecture to generate the URL to download extensions and, if it is running in the same Pod that is elected as primary, will set the `.status.primaryArch` in `SGCluster` if not already set.

WITH tabfreeze AS (
    SELECT pg_class.oid::regclass AS full_table_name,
    greatest(age(pg_class.relfrozenxid), age(toast.relfrozenxid)) as freeze_age,

ORDER BY 4 DESC;

Log4j2 Vulnerability "Log4Shell" analysis in relation to StackGres
# Background
An exploit for a critical zero-day vulnerability affecting Apache Log4j2 (CVE-2021-44228) known as Log4Shell was disclosed on December 10, 2021. All versions of Log4j2 versions >= 2.0-beta9 and <= 2.14.1 are affected by this vulnerability. This vulnerability is actively being exploited in the wild and allows an attacker to execute code on a remote server; a so-called Remote Code Execution (RCE).

There are many blogs posts and articles that explain the Log4Shell vulnerability, so it's not worth explaining it one more time, please read the following if you wish to know more:
* https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-44228
* https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/security.html
* https://blog.cloudflare.com/inside-the-log4j2-vulnerability-cve-2021-44228/
* https://snyk.io/blog/log4j-rce-log4shell-vulnerability-cve-2021-4428/
* https://blog.checkpoint.com/2021/12/11/protecting-against-cve-2021-44228-apache-log4j2-versions-2-14-1/

# Is StackGres affected by this vulnerability?
The short answer is: NO.

The StackGres platform uses Quarkus as the framework for developing the core components of the operator, and internally, Quarkus uses JBoss Log Manager and the JBoss Logging facade.

* https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/discussions/22108

Currently, StackGres makes use of `SLF4J` API that routes the log messages through `org.jboss.slf4j:slf4j-jboss-logmanager` to the JBoss logging library used by Quarkus, and that library is not affected by the Log4Shell vulnerability.

We do have declared the log4j2 dependency, but only with `test` scope, it's not included in the final, distributed images, and also the test configuration is using `nolookups` that disables this vulnerability and logs the message string untouched. And even then, the log4j dependency was actually not being used directly in any part of StackGres, so the next step is to simply drop the dependency declaration from StackGres since it's not used at all.

# Summary
* StackGres is **NOT** affected by this vulnerability since it uses the Quarkus Logging library instead of Log4j.
* If **your** application does use log4j, please follow the mitigation steps like the upgrade to Log4j v2.16.0+
* This issue is used to track the drop of log4j in the `test` scope since it's not used at all and will be closed once all the references to log4j are deleted from the main repo.

Re-implement SGDbOps for minor version upgrade operations
The operator already handle smoothly postgresql minor version upgrade. The operation will also perform the change of value in associated `SGCluster` CR to change the `.spec.postgresVersion` to the new value. 

> **NOTE** major pg version updates must be avoided since not supported. The operator have to print an error message requiring the intervention of the user to perform such update.

This action will be triggered by `SGDbOps` CRD (see #535) when `minorVersionUpgrade` operation is issued. Information about the process will be posted to the `status` field of the CR.

```yaml
spec:
  sgCluster: <string> # The name of sgcluster on which the operation will be performed
  op: <string> # minorVersionUpgrade
  schedule: <string> # An ISO 8601 date, that holds UTC scheduled date of the operation execution.
                     # If not specified or date it’s in the past it will be interpreted as ASAP.
  timeout: <string> # An ISO 8601 duration format `PnDTnHnMn.nS`, that specify a timeout after which the operation execution will not be performed.
                    # If the operation can not be performed due to timeout expiration the `.status.opStatus` field will be `timedout`.
                    # If not specified the operation will never fail for timeout expiration.
  maxRetries: <integer> # The maximum number of retries the operation is allowed to do after a failure. If not specified this default to `1`. Can not be greater than `10`.
  minorVersionUpgrade:
    postgresVersion: <string> # (required) the postgres version to upgrade (or downgrade) to
    method: <string> # (ReducedImpact | InPlace)
status:
  opStatus: <string> # (running | failed | timedout | completed)
  opRetries: <integer> # The number of retries performed by the operation
  minorVersionUpgrade:
    sourcePostgresVersion: <string> # The postgres version currently used by primary instance
    targetPostgresVersion: <string> # The postgres version that the cluster will be upgraded (or downgraded) to
    initialInstances: # The list of pods when this operation has been started
    - <string> # The pod name
    pendingToRestartInstances: # The list of pods that are pending to be restarted by this operation
    - name: <string> # The pod name
    restartedInstances: # The list of pods that have been restarted by this operation
    - name: <string> # The pod name
    switchoverInitiated: <string> # An ISO 8601 date indicating if and when the switchover took place
    failure: <string> # A failure message in case this operation has failed
```

Following validations of `SGDbOps` of type `minorVersionUpgrade` will apply:

* If specified `.spec.minorVersionUpgrade.postgresVersion` has different major version than the one specified by the associated `SGCluster` `.spec.postgresVersion` the validating webhook will return the error "minor version upgrade operation can not be used to upgrade to a PostgreSQL major version".

Following validations of `SGCluster` will apply:

* If `.spec.postgresVersion` is modified with a version that has the same major version than the previous the validating webhook will return the error "Use SGDbOps with `op = minorVersionUpgrade` to perform minor version upgrade of PostgreSQL".

Based on the backup restoration support (#176), we should augment the functionality to support [PITR](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/continuous-archiving.html). Add a new field to the `PostgresCluster` CRD, under the `clusterData` section, named `restoreToTimestamp`. It would look like:

clusterData:

Note that Postgres also supports specifying PITR by other concepts such as xid, label or LSN (see Postgres `recovery_target_*` parameters). Those are more low-level options and may not be supported for now.
